cancer_indication: PD-L1–positive unresectable locally advanced or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), and investigational use in other breast cancer subtypes
moa: Atezolizumab binds the immune checkpoint ligand PD-L1 (CD274) on tumor and immune cells and blocks its interaction with PD-1 and CD80, releasing inhibitory signals on cytotoxic T cells. In breast cancer, particularly PD-L1–positive TNBC with high tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes, this restores IFN-γ–driven T-cell activation, antigen presentation and cytotoxic killing of tumor cells rather than directly inducing tumor cell death. Efficacy depends on a pre-existing but restrained anti-tumor immune response; immune-excluded or immune-desert phenotypes with high TGF-β, Wnt or hypoxia signaling respond poorly despite PD-L1 blockade.

HALLMARK_INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE.description: Canonical interferon-gamma response program including IFN-γ–inducible chemokines (such as CXCL9, CXCL10), IDO1 and MHC antigen-presentation machinery.
HALLMARK_INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE.interpretation: In TNBC, high IFN-γ response marks a T cell–inflamed, PD-L1–induced state where antigen presentation and T-cell recruitment are active, predicting sensitivity to atezolizumab; loss of IFN-γ signaling (for example via JAK mutations) impairs MHC upregulation and contributes to resistance.

HALLMARK_ALLOGRAFT_REJECTION.description: T cell–mediated alloreactive immune response signature enriched for CD8+ T-cell, NK-cell activation and cytotoxic effector genes.
HALLMARK_ALLOGRAFT_REJECTION.interpretation: In breast cancer biopsies from atezolizumab-treated TNBC, enrichment of this T-cell cytotoxicity signature reflects dense effector T-cell infiltration and is associated with an immune-inflamed microenvironment and better clinical response.

WP_CANCER_IMMUNOTHERAPY_BY_PD1_BLOCKADE.description: Pathway capturing PD-1/PD-L1 immune checkpoint signaling and its blockade, encompassing PD-L1 expression on tumor and immune cells and PD-1 signaling on T cells.
WP_CANCER_IMMUNOTHERAPY_BY_PD1_BLOCKADE.interpretation: Atezolizumab directly targets this axis by binding PD-L1; tumors with active PD-1/PD-L1 signaling (PD-L1–positive TNBC with TILs) derive benefit from checkpoint release, whereas PD-L1–negative tumors lack the target and are primarily resistant.

HALLMARK_WNT_BETA_CATENIN_SIGNALING.description: Wnt ligand–driven β-catenin signaling controlling stemness, proliferation and stromal crosstalk.
HALLMARK_WNT_BETA_CATENIN_SIGNALING.interpretation: In TNBC tumor cells and cancer-associated fibroblasts, high Wnt/β-catenin activity excludes T cells from the tumor bed and can induce PD-L1 on stroma, creating an immune-cold, atezolizumab-resistant microenvironment; experimental Wnt inhibition restores T-cell infiltration and sensitivity.

HALLMARK_TGF_BETA_SIGNALING.description: Transforming growth factor-beta pathway regulating fibroblast activation, extracellular matrix deposition, EMT and immune suppression.
HALLMARK_TGF_BETA_SIGNALING.interpretation: TNBC basal-like immune-suppressed tumors with high TGF-β and EMT signatures exhibit dense stroma and peripheral T-cell trapping, conferring poor response to atezolizumab, whereas lower TGF-β activity and EMT downregulation are linked to immune-infiltrated, therapy-sensitive phenotypes.

GOBP_ANTIGEN_PROCESSING_AND_PRESENTATION.description: MHC class I and II antigen processing and presentation machinery including B2M, TAP transporters and HLA heavy chains.
GOBP_ANTIGEN_PROCESSING_AND_PRESENTATION.interpretation: Intact and upregulated antigen presentation in TNBC supports effective recognition of tumor neoantigens by T cells and correlates with better response to PD-L1 blockade; loss-of-function events such as B2M or JAK mutations downregulate this pathway and drive immune escape from atezolizumab.

GOBP_REGULATION_OF_T_CELL_ACTIVATION.description: Biological processes that positively or negatively regulate T-cell activation, including co-stimulatory and co-inhibitory receptor–ligand interactions and cytokine cues.
GOBP_REGULATION_OF_T_CELL_ACTIVATION.interpretation: Breast tumors with robust CD8+ T-cell activation and cytotoxic programs respond better to atezolizumab, while adaptive upregulation of alternative checkpoints (e.g. LAG-3, TIM-3) or deficient activating signals contributes to T-cell exhaustion and resistance.

HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.description: Oncogenic PI3K–AKT–mTOR survival and metabolism signaling downstream of growth factor receptors and PTEN loss.
HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.interpretation: In TNBC, hyperactive PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling (for example via PTEN loss or PIK3CA mutation) is linked to reduced TILs and an immunosuppressive cytokine milieu, mediating primary resistance to PD-L1 blockade; pharmacologic AKT inhibition has been explored to re-sensitize tumors to atezolizumab.

HALLMARK_HYPOXIA.description: Hypoxia-inducible factor–driven transcriptional response to low oxygen, including HIF1A targets and pro-angiogenic factors such as VEGF.
HALLMARK_HYPOXIA.interpretation: TNBC with strong hypoxia/angiogenesis signatures exhibit poor T-cell infiltration and inferior atezolizumab outcomes, whereas responders show relative downregulation of hypoxia programs on treatment, consistent with a more permissive immune microenvironment.

KEGG_HOMOLOGOUS_RECOMBINATION.description: DNA double-strand break repair by homologous recombination involving BRCA1, BRCA2 and associated repair factors.
KEGG_HOMOLOGOUS_RECOMBINATION.interpretation: Breast cancers with homologous recombination deficiency, including gBRCA1/2-mutated TNBC, accumulate neoantigens, display high TILs and PD-L1 expression and tend to be more sensitive to atezolizumab-based regimens, while restoration or upregulation of repair on treatment can represent a tumor survival response.

HALLMARK_TNFA_SIGNALING_VIA_NFKB.description: TNF-α–induced NF-κB inflammatory signaling driving cytokine and chemokine production.
HALLMARK_TNFA_SIGNALING_VIA_NFKB.interpretation: An immune-oriented TNFα/NF-κB profile that induces chemokines like CXCL9 and CXCL10 supports dendritic cell activation and T-cell recruitment and is associated with atezolizumab sensitivity, whereas tumor-intrinsic NF-κB survival and growth signals may counteract this benefit if dominant.

GOBP_KYNURENINE_METABOLIC_PROCESS.description: Metabolism of tryptophan along the kynurenine pathway, largely mediated by IDO1 in the tumor microenvironment.
GOBP_KYNURENINE_METABOLIC_PROCESS.interpretation: In TNBC, IFN-γ–induced IDO1 increases kynurenine and depletes tryptophan, suppressing T-cell proliferation; high IDO1/kynurenine activity marks resistance to PD-L1 blockade, and pharmacologic IDO inhibition is mechanistically expected to enhance atezolizumab efficacy.

GOBP_REGULATION_OF_T_CELL_COSTIMULATION.description: Regulation of co-stimulatory signals for T cells, including CD28–CD80/CD86 and cytokines such as IL-2.
GOBP_REGULATION_OF_T_CELL_COSTIMULATION.interpretation: Effective atezolizumab activity requires not only PD-L1 blockade but also adequate co-stimulation; breast tumors or microenvironments that downregulate CD80/86 or IL-2 signaling leave T cells anergic despite PD-L1 inhibition, contributing to clinical resistance.

sensitivity_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: High PD-L1 (CD274) expression on tumor-infiltrating immune cells or tumor cells identifies TNBC that are dependent on the PD-1/PD-L1 checkpoint for immune escape; in IMpassion130, PD-L1–positive tumors derived clear PFS benefit from atezolizumab plus nab-paclitaxel, making CD274 upregulation a predictive marker of sensitivity.

CXCL9 is an IFN-γ–inducible chemokine that recruits effector T cells; upregulation in TNBC corresponds to a T cell–inflamed microenvironment and has been linked to better responses to PD-1/PD-L1 blockade, supporting atezolizumab sensitivity when CXCL9 is high.

Similar to CXCL9, CXCL10 is induced by interferon signaling and promotes T-cell trafficking into tumors; high CXCL10 expression in TNBC is associated with robust immune infiltration and improved outcomes with checkpoint inhibition, consistent with greater benefit from atezolizumab.

CCL5 participates in recruiting T cells and dendritic cells; its upregulation, often as part of interferon/NF-κB inflammatory programs, marks immune-infiltrated TNBC that respond more favorably to PD-L1 blockade compared with chemokine-poor, immune-cold tumors.

sensitivity_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: Loss-of-function germline or somatic BRCA1 mutations cause homologous recombination deficiency, increasing genomic instability, neoantigen load and TILs; TNBC with BRCA1 deficiency have shown numerically higher response rates to checkpoint inhibitors and are highlighted as more immunogenic, indicating increased atezolizumab sensitivity when BRCA1 function is low.

BRCA2 deficiency similarly impairs homologous recombination and contributes to HRD-high status; BRCA2-mutated breast cancers can present with higher neoantigen burden and immune infiltration, and HRD-positive cohorts are described as more responsive to PD-L1 blockade, supporting increased atezolizumab sensitivity with BRCA2 loss.

resistance_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: LAG-3 upregulation on T cells is reported after PD-1/PD-L1 blockade in TNBC, providing an alternative inhibitory signal that maintains T-cell exhaustion even when PD-L1 is blocked; high LAG3 expression in this context is described as a resistance mechanism and has motivated trials combining LAG-3 and PD-L1 inhibitors.

HAVCR2 (TIM-3) is another checkpoint receptor that becomes upregulated on T cells following PD-1/PD-L1 inhibition; TNBC studies cited show increased TIM-3 on Tregs and CD4 T cells under PD-L1 blockade, contributing to continued T-cell dysfunction and resistance to atezolizumab.

CTLA4 expression on T cells provides a separate inhibitory axis during priming; although less extensively documented in breast cancer than in melanoma, the text notes that upregulated CTLA-4 can contribute to residual immune suppression and reduced benefit from PD-L1 blockade alone.

IDO1 is induced by IFN-γ and catalyzes tryptophan degradation into kynurenine; high IDO1 activity in TNBC creates a metabolically suppressive microenvironment that blunts T-cell proliferation, and tumors that upregulate IDO1 under immune pressure are described as more resistant to atezolizumab, prompting trials of IDO inhibition with checkpoint blockade.

IL-10 is an anti-inflammatory cytokine produced by tumors and tumor-associated myeloid cells; its increased expression dampens effector T-cell responses even when PD-L1 is blocked, and IL-10–rich environments are cited as part of immunosuppressive cytokine networks associated with poor checkpoint inhibitor responses.

VEGFA-driven angiogenesis is highlighted as both promoting hypoxia and directly inhibiting T-cell function and trafficking; high VEGF levels in hypoxic tumors correlate with poor responses to immunotherapy, which underlies combination strategies of anti-angiogenics with PD-L1 inhibitors to overcome this resistance mechanism.

HIF1A is a central transcription factor in the hypoxia program; high HIF-1α target-gene expression in atezolizumab-treated TNBC correlates with immune exclusion and inferior PFS, whereas responders show reduced hypoxia signatures, indicating that upregulated HIF1A activity contributes to resistance.

MYC amplification or overexpression in TNBC drives oncogenic transcriptional programs that suppress antigen presentation and foster immune evasion; preclinical data cited show that MYC-driven tumors are highly resistant to checkpoint blockade unless MYC-related processes are targeted, so MYC upregulation is considered a resistance biomarker to atezolizumab.

FOXP3 marks regulatory T cells; tumors with high FOXP3+ Treg infiltration have stronger immunosuppressive tone, and the document notes that high Treg-associated pathways reduce atezolizumab efficacy, making elevated FOXP3-expressing Tregs a resistance feature.

ARG1 is expressed by myeloid-derived suppressor cells and depletes arginine needed for T-cell proliferation; increased ARG1 expression is included among MDSC-associated pathways that accumulate under therapy and inhibit effector T cells, contributing to resistance to PD-L1 blockade.

IL-6 supports MDSCs and inflammatory but immunosuppressive myeloid phenotypes; the text reports that elevated IL-6 and IL-8 levels are associated with worse outcomes on immunotherapy, indicating that IL6 upregulation is part of Treg/MDSC immunosuppressive pathways that blunt atezolizumab benefit.

CCR4 is a chemokine receptor that attracts regulatory T cells; tumors with higher expression of CCR4-linked pathways recruit more Tregs, and the document notes that such Treg-enriched microenvironments reduce the effectiveness of atezolizumab.

CXCR2 mediates neutrophil and MDSC chemotaxis; upregulation of CXCR2-associated pathways brings suppressive myeloid populations into the tumor bed, and the text highlights CXCR2 blockade as a strategy to reduce MDSC recruitment and potentially restore sensitivity to PD-L1 blockade, implying that high CXCR2 activity marks resistance.

resistance_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: B2M encodes β2-microglobulin, essential for MHC class I surface expression; the document notes that B2M mutations and loss of MHC I antigen presentation are observed in resistant cases, meaning B2M downregulation or loss allows tumor cells to evade T-cell recognition despite atezolizumab-induced T-cell activation.

JAK1 transduces interferon-γ signaling in tumor cells; a truncating JAK1 mutation is reported in a non-responding TNBC, and loss of JAK-STAT signaling prevents IFN-γ–induced upregulation of MHC and PD-L1, thereby shielding tumor cells from immune attack and conferring resistance to PD-L1 blockade.

JAK2 mediates interferon receptor signaling; the text describes acquired JAK2 inactivation in melanoma as a mechanism of resistance via loss of antigen presentation and extrapolates that similar downregulation in breast cancer would likewise abrogate IFN-γ responses, contributing to atezolizumab resistance when JAK2 function is lost.

While PD-L1 presence is required for atezolizumab binding, the document emphasizes that PD-L1–negative TNBC did not benefit in IMpassion130, effectively making very low or absent CD274 expression a marker of primary resistance because the target checkpoint axis is not engaged in these tumors.
